c_profile: 32-bit int, 64-bit int64_t, two's-complement narrowing, arithmetic signed right shift; compile with -fwrapv at both -O0 and -O2. No host-undefined division inputs are normalized. FixedDiv tests exclude INT_MIN operands. Negative numerator left shifts are observed under these compiler builds, not claimed portable ISO C semantics.
pending: FixedDiv operands containing INT_MIN are explicitly rejected by Lean; their C abs behavior is undefined and DOS behavior remains unverified.
DOS executable and IWAD profiles are not pinned; no demo, full-tick, or pixel parity is established.

Connected player movement fixtures include map collision/sliding but omit sector/weapon actions, reaction-time delays, state animation ticks, and full thinker ordering. The viewer uses this movement core; its surrounding doors/combat remain prototype behavior.
Ticcmd demo serialization, low-resolution turn carry, mouse/joystick, and weapon/special input commands are pending.
Collision fixtures exclude missile/skull effects, spechit overflow, thing-contact abs(INT_MIN), and validcount rollover.
Move callbacks test invocation order and immediate scene changes, not actual DOOM special actions. Nested position queries that overwrite global spechit scratch remain outside the callback domain.

Path and slide checks reject unverified abs(INT_MIN) inputs and intercepts beyond the 128-entry original buffer. Historical memory-overrun emulation is pending. Read-only traversal visitors only; slide fixtures record special callbacks without implementing actual sector actions. Collision/slide now feed horizontal friction and ordered player movement traces, and the viewer uses that core. This is not full-tick or demo parity.

Pickup effects now run during ordered movement contact in the fixtures and runtime, with immediate unlinking and effects retained after failed moves. Multiplayer persistence, DeHackEd values, original audio, pending-weapon consumption, thinker deletion and item respawn remain outside these fixtures. The runtime bridges prototype combat inventory and uses medium skill, commercial for MAP-prefixed maps.

Live counter ticking runs before movement contacts in the runtime. Full PlayerThink action ordering and DeathThink are not ported; damage-counter production and display remain prototype combat behavior. Power colormaps now apply to opaque rendering, with the sky exception. High-detail fuzz now uses indexed buffers and persistent renderer phase for spectres and invisible weapons. Low-detail drawing, other viewport origins, vanilla projection/post rounding, BSP sprite visitation/ties, original palette flashes and complete rasterizer parity remain pending.

Status UI supports single-player STBAR full-refresh drawing at 320x32 with a 320x168 view. DOOM 1.0 split bars, multiplayer/frags, view-size controls, original incremental dirty-widget effects on unusual patch overlaps, HUD messages, menus, and intermissions remain pending. Number draw positions, palette selection and face state are independently checked, not whole-frame DOS parity. Face attacker bearings are supplied to this oracle; runtime uses the separately verified fixed-point angle core over prototype actors. Combat produces damage counters and remembered attackers but full P_DamageMobj and DeathThink remain unported.

Sector lighting covers map-spawned specials 1/2/3/4/8/12/13/17, original countdowns, short writes and shared random order. Walkover lighting 12/13/17/35/104/79/80/81 executes immediately during player movement; light switch use actions and general thinker insertion/removal/interleaving remain pending. The specialdata adapter represents doors and the two E1M1 floor/platform kinds; other sector movers remain pending. Actor spawning retains original imp draws but omits other original actor RNG consumption, and actor/door updates are not vanilla thinkers; independent lighting parity is not full-map RNG, tic, demo or pixel parity. Special 4 retains its damage marker but sector damage remains unported.

Moving-plane and vertical-door kernels match original code with supplied P_ChangeSector replies. Runtime doors use non-crushing sector changes with original block bounds, actor traversal and corpse/drop policy. Crush damage/blood, original EV door spawning/use dispatch, sound playback, and general thinker timing/lifetime remain pending. Existing runtime door targets and speeds use whole map units. Delayed/close-then-open types are kernel-tested but not yet spawned by runtime map actions.

Non-crushing sector changes retain height, gib and pickup/removal effects across tentative/rollback queries. Gib state requests are observed (S_GIBS has no action); removal uses original unlinking without thinker deletion, respawn queues or audio. Actor damage comes from prototype combat; supported deaths now use P_KillMobj and original death-state chains. Non-imp missile/skull query effects, crush=true damage and blood spawning, complete actor flags/state lifetimes and thinker order remain pending; this is not a complete P_ChangeSector or full-tick port.

Use ray traversal is now original and wired to runtime action dispatch. P_UseSpecialLine case 11 is reference-tested; other action bodies and door spawning remain prototype adapters; original PlayerThink use ordering and playback of sfx_noway are pending. The special-48 scrolling loop runs after map thinkers in runtime, but general thinker/button ordering, animated flat/texture translations and full rendering parity remain pending.

E1M1 floor 36 and lift 88 are integrated into player crossing callbacks and real non-crushing sector clipping. New floor/platform thinkers can tick on their activation tic; they retain insertion order among themselves. General actor/door/light/mover interleaving, non-imp monster movement crossing dispatch and unsupported manual-door interactions with active non-door thinkers remain unported. The kernel verifies nonplayer/projectile trigger gates; current runtime crossings are driven by the player and imps. Sound requests are recorded, not played. Other floor/platform kinds, stasis activation, and crusher damage remain pending. Runtime map heights use whole units for these whole-unit-speed actions; raw fractional kernel cases are independently tested.

Secret counting uses exact sector-floor equality and runs before player XY/Z movement; the live-player runtime gate is applied. Sector damage, original PlayerThink counter/use ordering and complete thinker interleaving remain pending. Normal exit switch 11 clears its special and queues completion even without a matching texture. The activation tic finishes; subsequent gameplay holds at the explicit unimplemented G_DoCompleted/WI_Ticker boundary. This is not an intermission, next-map transition, complete-level run or demo parity. The switch sound ID is checked, but the historical buttonlist[0].soundorg pointer and sound playback are outside the fixture. Runtime switch mode uses normal base-archive map markers; unusual IWAD/version identification remains outside the supported profile.

Original hitscan/autoaim is wired to player pistol and existing hitscan enemies using live BLOCKMAP links and fixed-point actor heights. Shoot specials 24/46/47 are explicitly rejected when applicable; E1M1 has none. The read-only kernel records special/impact/damage requests; mutating shoot-special callbacks must be integrated before broader map compatibility. Blood/puff actor spawning, effect RNG consumption/lifetimes/rendering and P_DamageMobj remains unported; supported P_KillMobj death actions are now ported. Damage still uses the prototype adapter, while unsupported monsters still absorb shots without damage actions; no full attack/tic/RNG parity is claimed. Non-imp enemy sight/chase/targeting and attack/weapon scheduling remain prototypes. Imp actions and shadow aim now have separate C comparisons. Missing two-sided backsector emulation, nonpositive attack ranges and previously excluded path arithmetic/overflows remain outside this oracle domain.

Death-state parity covers the player, zombieman, shotgunner, demon, imp and barrel chains. P_KillMobj emits drop/weapon/automap requests in the oracle; runtime drops retain original item-spawn RNG consumption, but general P_SpawnMobj/lifetime/thinker insertion is not ported. DeathThink, actual P_DropWeapon psprite lowering, corpse momentum/gravity/friction, nightmare respawn, other monster deaths, sound playback and full thinker order remain pending. Kill/frag accounting for nonplayer and network sources is kernel-tested, not multiplayer gameplay. No full damage/attack/tic/RNG parity is claimed.

Imps use original normal-speed single-player look/chase/face/melee/missile actions, original live/pain/death states and imp-fireball spawning/collision. Runtime adds persistent sector hearing, original BSP sight, fixed-point monster movement and selected manual-door gates. Barrels take damage, retain the first surviving-hit target, explode on the original A_Explode frame, affect supported actors/player and chain through delayed states, then unlink at S_NULL. Radius sight is now original BSP/REJECT traversal, while imp AI now uses the same original sight path; other enemy AI sight remains the old adapter. P_DamageMobj thrust/threshold/infighting generally remains pending; barrel target retention is a selected bridge. Radius request collection assumes damage does not relocate actors or trigger an immediate nested blast in this adapter. Full callback/reentrant thinker parity, corpse and barrel motion, unsupported monster damage and actual audio remain pending. Sight fixtures exclude short REJECT/invalid BSP memory emulation and undefined abs/division inputs.

Imp action fixtures supply movement and sight responses; runtime composition is tested separately. Multiplayer/fast/nightmare branches, full P_DamageMobj thrust and general infighting, complete actor spawn RNG and global thinker order remain pending. Fireballs update in creation order after actors; this is not original global interleaving. Monster door gates/reopening use the existing door allocation adapter. Runtime regressions cover projectile travel/dodging, wall impacts and rendering; floor/ceiling/sky paths do not yet have independent movement-oracle coverage. This is not complete P_MobjThinker/rasterizer parity. Sound requests are recorded, not played.
